title: Frog Fights
statementMd:
Ostap Bender recently visited frog farm and was inspired to create his own frog game.

Number of frogs are places on a cyclic gameboard, divided into $*m*$ cells. Cells are numbered from $1$ to $*m*$, but the board is cyclic, so cell number $1$ goes right after the cell number $*m*$ in the direction of movement. $*i*$-th frog during its turn can jump for $*a*_{*i*}$ cells.

Frogs move in turns, game starts with a move by frog $1$. On its turn $*i*$-th frog moves $*a*_{*i*}$ cells forward, knocking out all the frogs on its way. If there is a frog in the last cell of the path of the $*i*$-th frog, that frog is also knocked out. After this the value $*a*_{*i*}$ is decreased by the number of frogs that were knocked out during this turn. If $*a*_{*i*}$ is zero or goes negative, then $*i*$-th frog doesn't make moves anymore.

After frog number $1$ finishes its turn, frog number $2$ starts to move, then frog number $3$ and so on. After the frog number $*n*$ makes its move, frog $1$ starts to move again, then frog $2$ and so on this process goes forever. If some frog was already knocked out from the board, we consider that it skips all its moves.

Help Ostap to identify, what frogs will stay on the board at the end of a game?

## Input

First line of the input contains two integers $*n*$ and $*m*$ ($1 ≤ *n* ≤ 100000, 1 ≤ *m* ≤ 10^{9}, *n* ≤ *m*$) — number of frogs and gameboard size, respectively.

Following $*n*$ lines contains frogs descriptions — two integers $*p*_{*i*}$ and $*a*_{*i*}$ ($1 ≤ *p*_{*i*}, *a*_{*i*} ≤ *m*$) — the number of cell occupied by $*i*$-th frog initially and initial jump length. All $*p*_{*i*}$ are guaranteed to be distinct.

## Output

In the first line output number of frogs on the final gameboard. In the second line output their numbers in any order.

## Note

In the first sample first frog jumps $1$ cell and finishes in cell number $3$. Second frog jumps for $3$ cells and finishes on cell number $3$, knocking out frog number $1$. Current jump length for frog number $2$ is now $2$. Third frog jumps to cell $2$, then second frog jumps to cell $5$. Third frog in turn finishes in cell $5$ and removes frog $2$ from the gameboard. Now, it's the only remaining frog in the game.

In the second sample first frog jumps $2$ cells and knocks out frogs in cells $2$ and $3$. Its value $*a*_{*i*}$ is now $0$. Then fourth frog jumps and knocks out fifth frog and its $*a*_{*i*}$ is now $0$ too. These two frogs will remains on the gameboard forever.
statementZhMd:
奥斯塔普·本德尔最近参观了一家青蛙养殖场，并受到启发，决定制作自己的青蛙游戏。

游戏棋盘上放置着若干只青蛙，棋盘由 $*m*$ 个格子组成。格子编号从 $1$ 到 $*m*$，但棋盘是环形的，因此沿移动方向，编号为 $1$ 的格子紧接在编号为 $*m*$ 的格子之后。第 $*i*$ 只青蛙在其回合可以跳跃 $*a*_{*i*}$ 个格子。

青蛙轮流行动，游戏从青蛙 $1$ 的行动开始。在自己的回合中，第 $*i*$ 只青蛙向前移动 $*a*_{*i*}$ 个格子，并击倒沿途经过的所有青蛙。如果第 $*i*$ 只青蛙移动路径的最后一个格子中有青蛙，那么这只青蛙也会被击倒。之后，$*a*_{*i*}$ 的值会减去本回合中被击倒的青蛙数量。如果 $*a*_{*i*}$ 变为零或负数，那么第 $*i*$ 只青蛙将不再移动。

青蛙 $1$ 完成回合后，青蛙 $2$ 开始行动，接着是青蛙 $3$，依此类推。青蛙 $*n*$ 行动后，青蛙 $1$ 再次开始行动，然后是青蛙 $2$，如此无限进行。如果某只青蛙已经被击倒离开棋盘，则认为它会跳过之后的所有回合。

请帮助奥斯塔普确定游戏结束时哪些青蛙仍留在棋盘上。

## 输入格式

输入的第一行包含两个整数 $*n*$ 和 $*m*$（$1 ≤ *n* ≤ 100000, 1 ≤ *m* ≤ 10^{9}, *n* ≤ *m*$），分别表示青蛙数量和棋盘大小。

接下来的 $*n*$ 行描述青蛙的信息，每行包含两个整数 $*p*_{*i*}$ 和 $*a*_{*i*}$（$1 ≤ *p*_{*i*}, *a*_{*i*} ≤ *m*$），分别表示第 $*i*$ 只青蛙初始所在的格子编号和初始跳跃长度。保证所有 $*p*_{*i*}$ 互不相同。

## 输出格式

第一行输出最终棋盘上剩余的青蛙数量。

第二行以任意顺序输出它们的编号。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，第一只青蛙跳跃 $1$ 个格子，最终停在编号为 $3$ 的格子中。第二只青蛙跳跃 $3$ 个格子，最终也停在编号为 $3$ 的格子中，并击倒了第一只青蛙。此时第二只青蛙的跳跃长度变为 $2$。第三只青蛙跳到编号为 $2$ 的格子，随后第二只青蛙跳到编号为 $5$ 的格子。第三只青蛙行动时最终停在编号为 $5$ 的格子中，并将第二只青蛙从棋盘上移除。此时它成为游戏中唯一剩下的青蛙。

在第二个样例中，第一只青蛙跳跃 $2$ 个格子，并击倒了位于编号为 $2$ 和 $3$ 的格子中的青蛙。此时它的 $*a*_{*i*}$ 值变为 $0$。随后第四只青蛙行动，击倒了第五只青蛙，它的 $*a*_{*i*}$ 值也变为 $0$。这两只青蛙将永远留在棋盘上。
